title: Sample idea: let an agent approve small refunds
idea: An AI agent approves every customer refund under $50 without a person.

rounds.name: Blind positions
notes: Who gains from gaming a no-questions refund? Expect the rate to climb.
Most small refunds wait days for a two-minute check. That wait is the real cost.
Customers who are refused need a person to appeal to.
What share of past small refunds were wrong? Without that number this is a guess.
Go further: refund instantly at the moment of complaint.
Plan for the day the agent is fooled a thousand times in an hour.
rounds.card: An agent approves refunds under $50, with a daily cap and a human appeal path.

rounds.name: Cross-examination
notes: Try it on one product line for a month before all of them.
Set a hard daily spending ceiling the agent cannot raise.
Tell the customer plainly that an agent decided, and how to reach a person.
Refund data should flow back to product teams, or the cause never gets fixed.
rounds.card: For one product line, an agent approves refunds under $50, up to a daily cap, tells the customer an agent decided, and offers a human appeal. Reasons go back to the product team.

rounds.name: Vote
notes: Faster help for many, with a cap on the harm.
Watch for organized abuse once word spreads.
rounds.card: Same, plus a fraud check that pauses the agent if refunds spike.

gates.finding: Rules fit in the existing refund system.
A spike could drain money before anyone notices.
gates.change: Pause automatically above 3x the normal hourly rate.

gates.finding: Cap limits the worst month to a known number.

gates.change: Every refusal links to a person within one business day.

final: For one product line, an agent approves refunds under $50 up to a daily cap. It pauses itself if refunds run 3x above normal, says plainly that an agent decided, and links every refusal to a person within one business day. Refund reasons go to the product team weekly.
changed: Limited to one product line first
Daily cap and automatic pause on spikes
Plain notice that an agent decided
Human appeal within one business day
dissent: The Economist still expects the refund rate to rise once customers learn the rule, and wants it measured before any expansion.
